Each question appears twice: **SymPy** first, then **Maxima**. Both copies use the same question, options, seed and variants. Choose the same variant number in both copies to compare their assessment. Answers, validation, feedback and reset are independent.

Press **Validate answers** to inspect each interpreted response, then **Check answer** to grade it. After an edit, validate again. The first assessment loads that backend; Maxima can take longer to initialize.

The [native questions and graphical answers](native.qmd) page also demonstrates native question preparation, input validation and response trees, with optional PythonChecker nodes.

## Which questions need CTM?

**11 questions use standard STACK features; 7 require CTM extensions.** There are **3 unchanged upstream questions** and **15 questions authored or adapted for CTM**.

| Question source and features | Count | Questions | Stock STACK status |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Unchanged upstream STACK XML | 3 | AlgMap-6.1, BODMAS, rounding | Standard STACK features; the source XML matches the pinned upstream copies. |
| CTM-authored, standard STACK features | 8 | Rational expression, hyperbolic equivalence, numerical checks, zero-product equations, Boolean equivalence, finite lists/sets, nested collections, finite author helpers | No CTM-only checker, author helper or input extension detected. |
| CTM PythonChecker extension | 6 | Determinant-one matrix, combined positive-definiteness test, separate symmetry/positivity tests, nullspace bases B and C, positive integer multiple | Requires the CTM Python checker; these files do not run unchanged in stock STACK. |
| CTM matrix input extension, standard grading | 1 | Rank and pivot columns of B | `AlgEquiv` is standard; adapt the custom resizable matrix configuration for stock STACK. |

::: {.callout-important}
**PythonChecker means the same Python grading in both columns.**

The six PythonChecker questions use the same supplied Python functions through Pyodide in the SymPy and Maxima copies. Every answer-test node in those six questions is a PythonChecker node: **none is graded by native Maxima**. The column names select the surrounding backend; they do not turn Python into Maxima.

The two nullspace questions also use CTM's `nullspace_basis(A)` author helper and its resizable matrix input. The rank/pivot question uses that input extension without a PythonChecker.
:::

These labels classify the question XML and its required features. **A complete import and run in stock Moodle/STACK has not been verified here.** Both columns on this page use CTM's frontend, validation and response-tree controller. The Maxima copy delegates ordinary STACK answer-test nodes to the pinned STACK library; its PythonChecker nodes stay in Python.

Read the [question-by-question source audit](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-wasm-maxima/blob/research/2026-10-runtime-feasibility/reports/reviewer-site/question-compatibility.json) for the pinned evidence and extension list.

## For teachers

Choose a question to try, then change the response to see which mathematical distinctions its grading preserves. The [authoring guide](https://erasmus-ctm.github.io/stack-sympy/docs/authoring.html) explains how to bring your own questions to a page.

### Algebraic equivalence and written form

**Standard STACK features | CTM-authored question.**

The prompt states the domain $x\ne -n$. A cancelled fraction and the original unreduced expression both receive full credit because the question asks for *any equivalent expression* on that domain. A reciprocal triggers a targeted feedback branch.

### Numerical answers and precision

#### Three numerical checks

**Standard STACK features | CTM-authored question.**

These fields demonstrate absolute tolerance, relative tolerance, and decimal-place precision. The final field distinguishes `17.5` from `17.50`, because the written precision is part of the task. Their response trees contribute 30%, 40%, and 30% of the total.

::: {#measurement-context .ai-context}
For a measured quantity, absolute tolerance compares $|x-a|$ to a fixed bound. Relative tolerance compares it to a fraction of the reference value. Written decimal places express the precision of a reported measurement.
:::

### Matrix conditions

#### Find a nonidentity matrix with determinant one

**CTM extension required: PythonChecker. Python grades this question in both columns; Maxima executes no native answer-test node.**

Enter **any integer $2\times2$ matrix with determinant 1, except the identity**.
Each of the three conditions earns one third of the score: integer entries,
determinant one, and nonidentity. You are finding a matrix that satisfies
conditions, rather than copying a displayed model answer.

#### A positive definite matrix {#symmetric-positive-definite-matrix}

**CTM extension required: PythonChecker. Python grades this question in both columns; Maxima executes no native answer-test node.**

Give any real symmetric or complex Hermitian positive definite $2\times2$
matrix, using integers or exact fractions for both real and imaginary
parts. Enter `%i` for $i$. The identity,
$\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$ and
`matrix([2,%i],[-%i,2])` all pass. The combined `is_hpd` checker makes one
decision and its response tree awards full credit only when both Hermitian
symmetry and positivity hold. Compare this with the separate-check
question below; the [teacher explanation](https://erasmus-ctm.github.io/stack-sympy/docs/python-checker-api.html#symmetric-positive-definite-matrices)
shows the exact mathematical test.

#### A basis for the null space of B

**CTM extension required: PythonChecker. Python grades this question in both columns; Maxima executes no native answer-test node.** It also requires CTM's `nullspace_basis(A)` author helper and bounded resizable matrix input. Both need adaptation for stock STACK.

Put one proposed basis vector in each column. A basis is not a unique matrix:
changing a vector’s nonzero scale can still give a correct answer. Choose the
number of columns before validating. The checker uses the original matrix
$B$ to define the space, so another independent basis is accepted.

#### A basis for the null space of C

**CTM extension required: PythonChecker. Python grades this question in both columns; Maxima executes no native answer-test node.** It also requires CTM's `nullspace_basis(A)` author helper and bounded resizable matrix input. Both need adaptation for stock STACK.

Here you may reorder or combine basis vectors, provided your columns remain
independent and span the null space of $C$. Entry-by-entry equality with one
model matrix would reject many correct answers. The checker uses the
original matrix $C$ to define the target space.

[Download XML](questions/course-c-nullspace.xml)

For both basis questions, **green** marks a nonzero vector in the target space
when the valid submitted vectors are independent. A green family can still be
incomplete. **Yellow** marks every member of a dependent valid family;
**red** marks a zero vector or one outside the space. The whole answer earns
credit only when it is a complete basis. Colors explain the result but do not
award partial marks. Editing or resizing clears them.

Read [how to author a basis question](https://erasmus-ctm.github.io/stack-sympy/docs/python-checker-api.html#basis-questions-use-the-matrix-in-the-question)
or [configure its matrix input](https://erasmus-ctm.github.io/stack-sympy/docs/matrix-input.html).

## Startup and response times {#startup-and-response-times}

### Frozen public measurements: milestone 3

**The hybrid Maxima worker now defers native startup until its first ordinary Check.**
On the measured build, first Validate took **5.99 s**, while first Check took **38.45 s**
including **38.40 s** of deferred Maxima/STACK initialization. Later Checks took **42 ms**.
Validation still uses Python in both columns. A PythonChecker-only question does not
start Maxima.

These frozen measurements describe deployed source **`15fa33299d68d64e122a2661a2868feb30130edb`**,
measured on **22 October 2026** by [benchmark attempt 2](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-wasm-maxima/actions/runs/39831459804/attempts/2). Subsequent page edits
do not rerun or relabel this batch. The workload is the first rational-expression
question, variant 1, with the same accepted answer in both columns.

Values are **median / minimum / maximum**. First-call rows have **3 samples per backend**;
warm rows have **15 samples per backend**, five calls in each of three fresh processes.

| Interval | SymPy | Hybrid Maxima |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First Validate: UI (s) | 5.901 / 5.899 / 5.944 | 5.992 / 5.931 / 6.315 |
| Worker initialization (s) | 5.715 / 5.710 / 5.755 | 5.805 / 5.742 / 6.131 |
| First Validate: worker RPC (ms) | 186.53 / 183.96 / 187.32 | 184.38 / 182.02 / 187.16 |
| Warm Validate: UI (ms) | 11.79 / 9.77 / 12.33 | 12.15 / 11.25 / 12.45 |
| First Check after validation: UI (s) | 0.011 / 0.011 / 0.012 | 38.446 / 38.178 / 38.964 |
| First Check: worker RPC (s) | 0.009 / 0.009 / 0.010 | 38.444 / 38.175 / 38.962 |
| Warm Check: UI (ms) | 11.71 / 10.02 / 12.98 | 42.26 / 40.49 / 46.85 |
| Warm Check: worker RPC (ms) | 10.80 / 9.06 / 12.17 | 41.41 / 39.71 / 45.85 |

For hybrid Maxima, deferred native initialization alone was **38.401 / 38.129 / 38.919 s**
(3 samples). It is included in first Check and its worker RPC; these intervals must not
be added together. First Check follows six validations, so it is the first native grade,
not a cold page or a cold Python worker.

**UI time** runs from the actual button click to the verdict DOM update. **Worker RPC**
time runs from the real worker message to its response. Initialization is recorded
separately and is included in the relevant first UI operation. Page navigation, HTML
loading, isolation bootstrap, answer entry and later MathJax painting are outside these
button intervals.

The [native assessment page](native.qmd#public-startup-and-response-times) measures the
different path where native STACK also prepares questions, validates inputs and runs
response trees. Its warm grading is more expensive than this page's hybrid answer-test
delegation; the two controllers should not be treated as identical workloads.

### Method and limits

The runner used Chromium **141.0.7390.37** on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu,
**4 virtual CPUs**. Each backend had three fresh Chromium processes,
profiles and workers. Each started with Validate and zero prior assessment RPCs, then
five warm validations, its first grade and five warm grades. Backend order alternated.
OS and CDN caches were not cleared; provenance fetches can warm CDN caches.

The benchmark verified the exact final browser navigation HTML and public asset
fingerprints, then checked HTML/assets again after the samples. See the
[frozen summaries, sample times, hashes and provenance](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-wasm-maxima/tree/research/2026-10-native-stack/reports/milestone-three/timings/39831459804-attempt-2/) and the
[timing evidence guide](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-wasm-maxima/blob/research/2026-10-native-stack/reports/milestone-three/timings/README.md).
This is one accepted answer on one runner, not a device/network benchmark, a confidence
interval or evidence of a general performance advantage. Ordinary functional builds
leave these statistics frozen.

### Historical milestone 2 baseline

The original eager-start build waited for Python and Maxima together: first Maxima
Validate was **43.28 s**, including **43.10 s** of worker initialization; warm Validate
was about **12.4 ms**. SymPy first Validate was **5.95 s**. Those are historical values
from [run 39759255662](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-wasm-maxima/actions/runs/39759255662),
with [its original report](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-wasm-maxima/tree/research/2026-10-runtime-feasibility/reports/reviewer-site/timings/39759255662).
They used an earlier build and run, so the change between batches is not a controlled
speedup estimate.

Later questions, variant changes and Reset reuse the loaded worker. Reloading creates
new workers; cached files can reduce download work while runtime initialization remains.

## For developers

Use the [authoring guide](https://erasmus-ctm.github.io/stack-sympy/docs/authoring.html) for imports, question options,
tests and AI Feedback policies. The [Python answer-test guide](https://erasmus-ctm.github.io/stack-sympy/docs/python-checker-api.html)
explains the basis and property choices and gives the complete
positive-definiteness checker walkthrough. The questions above link to their
XML; the positive-definiteness question also links to its Python file. The
rational activity chooses the `two-step-practice`
policy, while other feedback activities inherit a four-step sequence; see
[policy setup](https://erasmus-ctm.github.io/stack-sympy/docs/authoring.html#choose-a-teaching-policy). Run authored tests
and inspect alternate correct answers before publishing.
